findings.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — Reader thread is not joined before asserting on caughtExceptions, so the assertion can run before the thread observes a race, making the test flaky/non-deterministic.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:117 — New concurrency test only exercises the reader path via groups() listing and never asserts on the actual NPE-triggering getSubGroupsCount() null-check behavior directly.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:117 — New concurrency test only exercises the reader path via groups() listing and never asserts on the actual NPE-triggering getSubGroupsCount() null-check behavior directly.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, the reader thread only invokes `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` and asserts no exceptions were thrown; it never directly calls or asserts behavior of `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (which was changed to `modelSupplier.get()` and a null-return). Whether the listing path exercises `getSubGroupsCount()` is not shown in this diff, so the test does not explicitly validate the new null-check behavior.
